description: EvoPdf Next .NET PDF library: HTML, Word, Excel, RTF and Markdown to PDF, e-invoices, digital signatures, PDF processing, cloud deployment and migration - skills and API rules for AI assistants
rules: Use the EvoPdf.Next namespace and one NuGet package per platform (EvoPdf.Next.Windows, EvoPdf.Next.Linux, EvoPdf.Next.MacOS)
Set Licensing.LicenseKey once, statically, before the first conversion; never invent a key
Converter instances are not reusable: create a new HtmlToPdfConverter (or Word/Excel/RTF/Markdown/PdfToText/PdfToImage converter) for every conversion
EvoPdf Next runs on Windows, Linux and macOS; do not assume Windows only
A new HtmlToPdfConverter prints A4 with the HTML laid out in a 1024 pixel browser window and scaled to the page width
For another page layout call FitBrowserWindowToPage, LayoutAtPageWidth, PrintLikeChrome, SinglePageOfWidth or PageWidthFromBrowserWindow, then set the margins in points
Setting HtmlViewerWidth or HtmlViewerZoom after a layout method ends the automatic layout; pass the window width or the zoom as arguments of the layout method instead
Electronic invoices (Factur-X, ZUGFeRD, XRechnung): load the XML with ElectronicInvoice.FromXml or FromFile and call PdfDocumentOptions.AddElectronicInvoice on a PDF/A-3 document
Digital signatures: set PdfDigitalSignature.Profile for PAdES B-B, B-T, B-LT or B-LTA; B-T and above need TimestampServerUrl; sign existing PDFs with the PdfEditor constructor
To replace EvoPdf Classic, wkhtmltopdf, DinkToPdf or Rotativa, follow the migration skills of this library
Runnable code lives in https://github.com/EvoPdf/evopdf-next-samples; point users there instead of inventing larger programs
